title: Protein Extraction and Western Blotting Protocol
author: t.a.mcdougall
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bqubmwsn
materials: Whole cell protein was extracted from cells by treating cell pellets with Radio Immunoprecipitation Assay buffer (RIPA buffer: 1M NaCl, 1% NP-40, 0.5% sodium deoxycholate, 0.1%SDS, 50mM pH 7.4 Tris in ddH 2 O) was prepared according to the Cold Spring Harbor and supplemented with 1µl of Protease Inhibitor Cocktail from Roche per 100µl of RIPA buffer. RIPA buffer was added at a concentration of 500µl per ~2x10 6 cells.
The protein mixture was loaded into each well of the gel, and 5µl BenchMark Pre-stained Protein Ladder from Thermo Fisher was loaded into one of the wells abutting the samples.

The Bio Rad transfer holder cassette was arranged with the black frame (which would face the negative electrode) on one side and the clear frame (which would face the positive electrode) on the other. A foam pad from Bio Rad was placed on top of the black frame and upon that was placed a piece of the filter paper supplied in the Nitrocellulose/Filter Paper Sandwich from Thermo Fisher.

After blocking, the nitrocellulose was placed inside a 50ml falcon tube containing 20ml of primary antibody solution (3% w/v BSA, 0.1% v/v Tween-20 in TBS plus the relevant antibodies). The primary antibodies used in the cited study are shown here. steps.title: Extract Protein from Samples
steps.instruction: Break down cells and isolate the protein component from samples.

substeps.instruction: Gently agitate samples by shaking for 30 minutes at 4℃.
Centrifuge at max speed (>14,000 rcf) at 4℃ for 20 minutes.
Transfer the supernatant to a fresh microcentrifuge tube for immediate loading or store at -20℃.

steps.title: Prepare Gel Casting Plates
steps.instruction: Set up the casting apparatus and check for leaks.

substeps.instruction: Sandwich a 1.5mm glass spacer plate and cover plate together in a Bio Rad casting clamp and place on a gel casting stand.
Fill the plates with water and let sit for several minutes to ensure no leakage, then pour out the water.

steps.title: Cast the Lower Running Gel
steps.instruction: Prepare and pour the 12% acrylamide lower running gel.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 10ml of 12% acrylamide lower running gel by mixing 4.2ml of 29:1 acrylamide/bis-acylamide (Bio Rad), 2.5ml of 4x lower gel buffer (1.5M Tris and 0.4% SDS in distilled water, pH 8), and 3.3ml of distilled water.
Add 40µl of freshly prepared 10% ammonium persulfate and 10µl of TEMED (Fisher Scientific) to the mixture and mix thoroughly.
Immediately pour the solution into the casting plates to within 1cm of the top.
Fill the remaining 1cm of the plates with 100% isopropanol.
Allow the lower gel to solidify for at least 30 minutes.

steps.title: Cast the Upper Gel
steps.instruction: Prepare and pour the upper gel layer.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 3ml of upper gel mixture consisting of 0.75ml 29:1 acrylamide/bis-acylamide, 0.45ml of 4x upper gel buffer (0.5M Tris and 0.4% SDS in distilled water, pH 6.8), 1.8ml of distilled water, 10µl of 10% ammonium persulfate, and 5µl of TEMED (Fisher Scientific).
Pour off the isopropanol completely to expose the top of the lower gel.
Pour the upper gel mixture on top to fill the remaining centimeter of the plates.
Insert a 1.5mm gel comb into the top of the plates and allow the mixture to solidify for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Assemble Electrophoresis Tank
steps.instruction: Fit the gel into the electrode assembly and prepare the running buffer.

substeps.instruction: Remove the solid gel and glass case from the stand/clamp and fit into the Bio Rad electrode assembly with short plates facing inwards; remove the comb.
If running only one gel, insert a mock spacer plate and short plate combination on the opposite side (short plate inside) to create a watertight container.
Prepare 1 liter of Running buffer by diluting 100ml of 10x Running buffer (0.25M Tris, 1.92M Glycine, and 1% w/v SDS in distilled water) in 900ml distilled water.
Place the assembly into the Bio Rad buffer tank and fill to overflowing with the Running buffer.

steps.title: Prepare and Run Protein Samples
steps.instruction: Denature protein extracts and perform electrophoresis.

substeps.instruction: Mix 15µl of each protein extract with 2X SDS gel-loading buffer (4% SDS, 0.2% bromophenol blue, 20% glycerol, and 200mM dithiothreitol).
Heat the mixture to 95℃ for 2-3 minutes.
Run the gel at 180 volts until the bromophenol blue dye nearly reaches the bottom of the gel.
Ensure a significant gap remains between the bottom of the gel and the ~10kDa band of the Pre-stained Protein Ladder to prevent histones from running off.

steps.title: Prepare Transfer Buffer and Gel
steps.instruction: Prepare the buffer and equilibrate the gel for transfer.

substeps.instruction: Prepare Transfer buffer by combining 100ml of 10x Transfer buffer (0.25M Tris and 1.9M glycine in distilled water, stored at 4°C), 200ml of methanol, and 700ml of distilled water.
Remove the gel from the tank and assembly, then immerse it in cold Transfer buffer for 5 minutes.
Place the soaked gel on a piece of filter paper, ensuring it is fully supported and not touching the sponge beneath.
Briefly soak 0.2µm nitrocellulose in Transfer buffer, place it on top of the gel, and apply pressure with a smooth flat implement to remove gaps.
Pour a small amount of transfer buffer on top to ensure the nitrocellulose is completely soaked.
Cover the nitrocellulose with another piece of filter paper, then place a piece of spongy foam on top.
Fasten the clear frame over the black frame and fit the cassette into the Bio Rad Core Assembly Module with the black side of the cassette facing the black side of the module.

steps.title: Perform Protein Transfer
steps.instruction: Transfer proteins from the gel to the nitrocellulose membrane.

substeps.instruction: Insert the Core Assembly Module into the Bio Rad protein transfer tank with a cold ice pack.
Fill the tank with Transfer buffer and connect to a Bio Rad PowerPac HC power supply.
Carry out transfer at 90 volts for one hour at 4℃, using a magnetic stir bar for constant gentle agitation.

steps.title: Block the Membrane
steps.instruction: Block the membrane to prevent non-specific antibody binding.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the nitrocellulose membrane into 40ml of blocking buffer (TBS with 0.1% v/v Tween-20 and 3% BSA [1.2g BSA in 40ml TBS]).
Gently rock the membrane for one hour in the blocking buffer.

steps.title: Primary Antibody Incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the membrane with primary antibodies.

substeps.instruction: Incubate the membrane in the blocking solution overnight at 4℃ on a tube rotator.

steps.title: Wash and Secondary Antibody Incubation
steps.instruction: Wash the membrane and apply secondary fluorescent antibodies.

substeps.instruction: Wash the membrane four times for 5 minutes each in room temperature TBST (0.1% v/v Tween-20 in TBS) on a rocker.
Incubate the membrane for one hour at room temperature on a gently rocking rocker in 20ml of secondary antibody solution (3% w/v BSA, 0.1% v/v Tween-20 in TBS plus secondary antibody).
Use secondary fluorescent antibodies: Rabbit (LI-COR 925-68071 B81113-01, goat, 1:10,000) or Mouse (LI-COR 925-32210 926-32201, goat, 1:10,000).

steps.title: Final Wash and Imaging
steps.instruction: Perform final washes and image the membrane.

substeps.instruction: Wash the membrane twice with TBST and once in TBS for 5 minutes each at room temperature.
Image the membrane at relevant wavelengths using an LI-COR Odyssey machine (BioAgilytix) and Image Studio software.
